notes: California 1400, Audace, Eldorado, MGX-21 and the V85 TT. Ride-by-wire: there is no cable to the throttle bodies, so the handle (grip) and the throttle plates are learned as two separate routines and the order matters. The 7SM has no CO trim. Identification is confirmed to return Drawing / Hardware / Software / Omologation / Serial / Tester, and the session switches baud rate after init. Live local identifiers for this family have not been captured yet. Run the read-only identifier discovery scan and contribute the result; until then the workstation offers identification, DTCs and raw discovery only.

memory.write_blocked_reason: 7SM writing is the highest-risk operation in the Guzzi world and is not enabled in this build.
memory.hardware_note: Never run a 7SM write through a virtual machine - USB timing jitter has bricked ECUs.

routines.name: Handle (grip) self-learning
routines.description: Step 1 of 2 on ride-by-wire bikes. Learns the twistgrip sensor end stops. Ignition on, engine off, do not touch the grip while it runs.
routines.follow_up: Immediately run throttle self-learning. Leaving only the handle learned gives an inconsistent pair.
routines.warning: Must be followed by throttle self-learning before the bike is ridden.

routines.name: Throttle self-learning
routines.description: Step 2 of 2. Learns the motorised throttle plate end stops. Run immediately after handle self-learning.
routines.follow_up: Cycle the ignition, then verify the throttle tracks the grip smoothly before riding.

routines.name: Service interval reset
routines.warning: On most Guzzi models the service reset is done from the dashboard, not the ECU.
